title: A rehearsal's cold reader says it is the rehearsal
intention: The claude -p child a rehearsal spawns carries CAIRN_USER=rehearsal, so stripping CLAUDECODE never makes it Akien's hand.
why: Akien 2026-10-13 (verbatim at ideas/2026-10-13-so-lets-talk-first-about-the-cairn.json): "we set CAIRN_OPERATOR= this can be OPERATOR or Akien or whatever... Akien is a subclass of operator, and mostly this gets used for reporting... but when we use cairn superclaude or cairn cc0 or cairn librarian or whatever... we also set the otherwise unset variable CAIRN_USER= which can be librarian or cc0 or whatever. if CAIRN_USER is set, then it's you... if it's not, then it's me." He set export CAIRN_OPERATOR=Akien in ~/.bashrc (line 166) the same day. Measured 2026-10-13: rehearsal.py claude_reader (:414) strips CLAUDECODE from the environment to run claude -p outside the session, so the child carries neither marker and, once CAIRN_OPERATOR rides every shell, would read as Akien.
traces_to: Akien's spec verbatim in why, and Law 7 (no process may be recorded as Akien's hand by omission).
how: cairn/machines/rehearsal/rehearsal.py only: in claude_reader, after building env without CLAUDECODE, set env['CAIRN_USER'] = 'rehearsal'.
falsifier: cairn/machines/rehearsal/proofs/test_the_cold_reader_says_it_is_the_rehearsal.py under PROVES {'a135bdb13646': {'1','2'}} with subprocess.run monkeypatched to capture env and return a CompletedProcess whose stdout is a minimal JSON result: (1) the captured env has CAIRN_USER == 'rehearsal'; (2) it has no CLAUDECODE. Hollow: today's rehearsal.py reds 1.

decisions.text: The value is 'rehearsal', the machine's own name, as Akien's examples name the device ('librarian'). CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-12

The proof is pre-written and committed at cairn/machines/rehearsal/proofs/test_the_cold_reader_says_it_is_the_rehearsal.py (two teeth, subprocess.run monkeypatched, CLAUDECODE set and CAIRN_USER unset in the parent for the call); the builder runs it with bin/cairn test <path> and never edits it. Red first measured 2026-10-13: tooth 1 FAIL (CAIRN_USER=None), tooth 2 PASS. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED'

In cairn/machines/rehearsal/rehearsal.py claude_reader, on the line right after env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != 'CLAUDECODE'}, add env['CAIRN_USER'] = 'rehearsal' with a two-line comment naming ticket a135bdb13646; nothing else changes. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED'

Commit the build as 'a135bdb13646: build — ...', run the proof twice plus cairn/machines/rehearsal/proofs/test_rehearsal.py, seal, cross PROVEME with --proven-by cairn/machines/rehearsal/proofs/test_the_cold_reader_says_it_is_the_rehearsal.py, hollow-seal (bin/cairn test --hollow a135bdb13646 --seal), write the verdict against the validate berth, cross PROVED; cross.py writes the cursor back through the artifact door itself. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED'

Every command runs from ~/dev/src/cairn with the system python3 (PYTHONPATH=. python3 ...) or bin/cairn; there is no venv placeholder. 'The proof' is cairn/machines/rehearsal/proofs/test_the_cold_reader_says_it_is_the_rehearsal.py. Seal each run proof with bin/cairn test --seal <path>. The validate berth is ~/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets/validate-20261013T131405-5095ff9dc623.json. PROVED is crossed with PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m cairn.tools.base.cross a135bdb13646 PROVED --actor cc --why ... --proven-by <the proof>. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED'
